title: Cost of the LCFs' meaning: each side's candidates and the deep arms of exp-lcf-cost-deep-334, 100 training links
description: Chooses, on links the reports never use, the best configuration on each side of the question whether giving the latents a meaning costs anything, and the configuration of each deep arm of exp-lcf-cost-deep-334. Both sides keep expliCCit's encoder-decoder architecture exactly: an encoder of 1.27 million weights with seven outputs, read by an actor and a critic of two layers of 256. The meaningful side's encoder is neto1 v1, trained beforehand to output the seven LCFs; the free side's encoder starts from random weights and is trained by net2's objective. Training differs between the sides by design: the split lets the meaningful side train in stages (the encoder on ground truth, then the decision maker on the fixed encoder), while free latents have no target and can only be trained end to end by the decisions' loss, so each side is compared at its best rather than held to one method. Meaningful side (prefix split-): split-paper-imit (the actor cloned from BBRv3, lcft-paper-none, exp-lcf-cost-teacher-317) and split-paper-td3 (TD3+BC, lcftd-paper-a2.5-n60k, exp-lcf-cost-td3-326). Free side (prefix e2e-): e2e-free-imit (encoder and actor cloned from BBRv3 together, lcft-freefix-none, exp-lcf-cost-teacher-317) and e2e-free-td3 (TD3+BC with the encoder trained by the critic, lcftd-free-a2.5-n150k, exp-lcf-cost-td3-326). Not candidates, because they add a second 1.23-million-weight network between the seven LCFs and the actor: lcftd-deeppaper (on neto1 v1's estimates) and lcftd-deeptruth (on the true LCFs), the TD3+BC grid of exp-lcf-cost-deep-334 (alpha 2.5, 5 or 10 by 60,000 or 150,000 updates), which ask whether more capacity behind the LCFs would close the gap. Every policy runs on training seeds 0 and 1. A one-off in distribution: links 0 to 99 of net2's 600 training links, each under 2 of the data's 64 conditions drawn with campaign seed 31 (experiments/comfort.py), 30 s, every policy and BBRv3 on every episode. summary.md scores each policy in log utility per 10 ms step minus BBRv3, paired by link. chosen.json gives, by the mean over seeds, the best configuration of each side (split, e2e) and of each deep arm, never one with a failed episode in any seed. The choices are reported on links 100 onward and on unseen links, with and without competing flows. Nothing here supports a claim about any policy.
prepare: P=(); for a in "$IN"/n/lcftd-deep*-s[01]; do P+=(--policy "$(basename "$a")=$a/policy.onnx"); done; [ "${#P[@]}" -eq 48 ]; for s in 0 1; do P+=(--policy "split-paper-imit-s$s=$IN/t/lcft-paper-none-s$s/policy.onnx" --policy "e2e-free-imit-s$s=$IN/t/lcft-freefix-none-s$s/policy.onnx" --policy "split-paper-td3-s$s=$IN/p/lcftd-paper-a2.5-n60k-s$s/policy.onnx" --policy "e2e-free-td3-s$s=$IN/p/lcftd-free-a2.5-n150k-s$s/policy.onnx"); done; [ "${#P[@]}" -eq 64 ]; for x in "${P[@]}"; do [ "$x" = --policy ] || [ -f "${x#*=}" ]; done; uv run python experiments/comfort.py "$OUT/spec" --links 0:100 --seed 31 --stock bbr3 "${P[@]}"; uv run expliccit campaign plan "$OUT/spec/campaign.json" "$OUT/c-comfort"; cp "$OUT/spec/aliases.json" "$OUT/aliases.json"
run: for c in "$OUT"/c-*; do uv run expliccit campaign run "$c" --shard "$SHARD/$SHARDS" --build "$UML" --workers "$WORKERS" --tables steps; done; uv run python experiments/slim_steps.py "$OUT"
collect: uv run python experiments/rule_report.py "$OUT" --best split e2e lcftd-deeppaper lcftd-deeptruth --over-seeds
